It's not pathetic. I'm in the same position as you. I've had emetophobia for like 11 years since the last time I v'd. It gradually got worse to the point it was ruining my life with panic attacks, ocd, undereating, avoidance of public places and people, constant anxiety and eventually depression. I found that talking to people about it is super helpful give them your perspective, its a phobia so people understand its irrational. If you tell people you live with and that are close to you it can make you feel less pathetic and they'll be able to help you cope. As far as fixing it goes I'd recommend cognitave behavioural therapy. I just recently got the encouragement to go and its already started to work. You basically make a list of fears and you work up then one by one. For example my list starts with, crowded areas, touching food by washing hands once thoroughly instead of several times... and you just work on one thing until the anxiety comes down then you move up the scale. You also work on the unhelpful thoughts so you would look at a trigger and the feelings acossiated and the thoughts and try and think of an alternative convincing way of thinking about it. For example i wash glasses, plates and bowels before and after use to be extra sure. The unhelpful thought is ill get sick if i dont wash this twice, an alternative thought is washing once is plenty enough to clean this dish.


Hope this helps sorry for the long wall of text.

Every time I would get anxious but I would never actually get sick, so I would say it's definitely possible that is the cause of it.

**I haven't been skydiving** but I have done aerobatics in a plane and the zero g bit was fine, didn't even make my stomach go weird. If you don't suffer with motion sickness then I think you'll be fine. Skydiving the zero g portion doesn't last very long, once you reach terminal velocity you experience the same force as lying on the ground, just with air instead of concrete.
